A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LADM work. All 15 pages, including Appendices A–F, provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training experiments with perplexity, retrieval, and LongBench results, plus ablations and additional evaluations in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main evaluations, Table 6 ablations, and appendix evaluations in Tables 8–10.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Long Attention Calculator and PFS, AFS, and CDS selection procedure, including standard-deviation and distance weighting. No algorithm component or training objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Pile training domains, Proof-Pile perplexity evaluation, Needle-in-the-Haystack task, LongBench tasks, and Appendix F short-context benchmarks. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Random sampling and ProLong remain in the corresponding comparisons. Table 3 retains GPT-3.5-Turbo reference scores, and Table 10 retains the original short-context models; comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The preprocessing, 32K training sequences, model configurations, token budgets, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. The alternative training budgets and 1B-versus-5B calculator-training comparison already appear in v2.

E4.justification: Both retain the concatenation analysis, training-budget comparisons, stride sensitivity, weighting ablations, category-score analyses, and data examples. Appendices C–F contain the same supplementary analyses and findings.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 retains averaging across three experiments with different random-sampling seeds. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty reporting practices, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Corresponding results throughout the main text and appendices are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains Llama2-7B LADM's overall score of 37.83, and Table 9 retains 36.20 and 37.83 for 1B and 5B calculator-training tokens.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions in Equations 1–5 and computational-complexity expressions in Section 6.2 are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about attention-based dependency measurement, stronger long-context performance, and training efficiency with 1B tokens. Contribution scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of dependency scores and experimental findings are retained. The limitations still identify selector overhead, untested models above 13B parameters, and the restriction to 32K-context experiments.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix B retain the same hyperparameters, optimizer, training software, and implementation details. The code-availability footnote specifies the same repository.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 replaces Suri by Pham et al. (2024) with ACE-RL by Chen et al. (2025b), with corresponding bibliography removal and addition. The broader research positioning and comparison with ProLong are unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized editorial changes update citation labels, LR2Bench's bibliography title styling, and the arXiv version/date stamp. The prose, section sequence, and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The reference replacement causes limited bibliography reflow across pages 9–11. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–10 retain their designs, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: The peripheral citation substitution and minor presentation edits leave the method, experimental results, appendix evidence, and limitations intact. These changes do not materially strengthen or weaken the paper's scientific support, reproducibility, or clarity.
